methods.name: Open
methods.signature: Open(Filename As String, [UpdateLinks As Variant], [ReadOnly As Variant], [Format As Variant], [Password As Variant], [WriteResPassword As Variant], [IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended As Variant], [Origin As Variant], [Delimiter As Variant], [Editable As Variant], [Notify As Variant], [Converter As Variant], [AddToMru As Variant], [Local As Variant], [CorruptLoad As Variant]) As Workbook
methods.description: Opens a workbook.

parameters.name: Filename
parameters.description: String. The file name of the workbook to be opened.

parameters.name: UpdateLinks
parameters.description: Specifies the way external references (links) in the file, such as the reference to a range in the Budget.xls workbook in the following formula =SUM([Budget.xls]Annual!C10:C25), are updated. If this argument is omitted, the user is prompted to specify how links will be updated. For more information about the values used by this parameter, see the Remarks section. If Microsoft Excel is opening a file in the WKS, WK1, or WK3 format and the UpdateLinks argument is 0, no charts are created; otherwise, Microsoft Excel generates charts from the graphs attached to the file.

parameters.name: ReadOnly
parameters.description: True to open the workbook in read-only mode.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: If Microsoft Excel opens a text file, this argument specifies the delimiter character. If this argument is omitted, the current delimiter is used. For more information about the values used by this parameter, see the Remarks section.

parameters.name: Password
parameters.description: A string that contains the password required to open a protected workbook. If this argument is omitted and the workbook requires a password, the user is prompted for the password.

parameters.name: WriteResPassword
parameters.description: A string that contains the password required to write to a write-reserved workbook. If this argument is omitted and the workbook requires a password, the user will be prompted for the password.

parameters.name: IgnoreReadOnlyRecommended
parameters.description: True to have Microsoft Excel not display the read-only recommended message (if the workbook was saved with the Read-Only Recommended option).

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: If the file is a text file, this argument indicates where it originated, so that code pages and Carriage Return/Line Feed (CR/LF) can be mapped correctly. Can be one of the following XlPlatform constants: xlMacintosh, xlWindows, or xlMSDOS. If this argument is omitted, the current operating system is used.

parameters.name: Delimiter
parameters.description: If the file is a text file and the _Format_ argument is 6, this argument is a string that specifies the character to be used as the delimiter. For example, use Chr(9) for tabs, use "," for commas, use ";" for semicolons, or use a custom character. Only the first character of the string is used.

parameters.name: Editable
parameters.description: If the file is a Microsoft Excel 4.0 add-in, this argument is True to open the add-in so that it is a visible window. If this argument is False or omitted, the add-in is opened as hidden, and it cannot be unhidden. This option does not apply to add-ins created in Microsoft Excel 5.0 or later. If the file is an Excel template, True to open the specified template for editing. False to open a new workbook based on the specified template. The default value is False.

parameters.name: Notify
parameters.description: If the file cannot be opened in read/write mode, this argument is True to add the file to the file notification list. Microsoft Excel will open the file as read-only, poll the file notification list, and then notify the user when the file becomes available. If this argument is False or omitted, no notification is requested, and any attempts to open an unavailable file will fail.

parameters.name: Converter
parameters.description: The index of the first file converter to try when opening the file. The specified file converter is tried first; if this converter does not recognize the file, all other converters are tried. The converter index consists of the row numbers of the converters returned by the FileConverters property.

parameters.name: AddToMru
parameters.description: True to add this workbook to the list of recently used files. The default value is False.

parameters.name: Local
parameters.description: True saves files against the language of Microsoft Excel (including control panel settings). False (default) saves files against the language of Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) (which is typically United States English unless the VBA project where Workbooks.Open is run from is an old internationalized XL5/95 VBA project).

parameters.name: CorruptLoad
parameters.description: Can be one of the following constants: xlNormalLoad, xlRepairFile and xlExtractData. The default behavior if no value is specified is xlNormalLoad, and does not attempt recovery when initiated through the OM.

methods.name: OpenText
methods.signature: OpenText(Filename As String, [Origin As Variant], [StartRow As Variant], [DataType As Variant], [TextQualifier As XlTextQualifier], [ConsecutiveDelimiter As Variant], [Tab As Variant], [Semicolon As Variant], [Comma As Variant], [Space As Variant], [Other As Variant], [OtherChar As Variant], [FieldInfo As Variant], [TextVisualLayout As Variant], [DecimalSeparator As Variant], [ThousandsSeparator As Variant], [TrailingMinusNumbers As Variant], [Local As Variant])
methods.description: Loads and parses a text file as a new workbook with a single sheet that contains the parsed text-file data.

parameters.name: Filename
parameters.description: Specifies the file name of the text file to be opened and parsed.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Specifies the origin of the text file. Can be one of the following XlPlatform constants: xlMacintosh, xlWindows, or xlMSDOS. Additionally, this could be an integer representing the code page number of the desired code page. For example, "1256" would specify that the encoding of the source text file is Arabic (Windows). If this argument is omitted, the method uses the current setting of the File Origin option in the Text Import Wizard.

parameters.name: StartRow
parameters.description: The row number at which to start parsing text. The default value is 1.

parameters.name: DataType
parameters.description: Specifies the column format of the data in the file. Can be one of the following XlTextParsingType constants: xlDelimited or xlFixedWidth. If this argument is not specified, Microsoft Excel attempts to determine the column format when it opens the file.

parameters.name: TextQualifier
parameters.description: Specifies the text qualifier.

parameters.name: ConsecutiveDelimiter
parameters.description: True to have consecutive delimiters considered one delimiter. The default is False.

parameters.name: Tab
parameters.description: True to have the tab character be the delimiter (DataType must be xlDelimited). The default value is False.

parameters.name: Semicolon
parameters.description: True to have the semicolon character be the delimiter (DataType must be xlDelimited). The default value is False.

parameters.name: Comma
parameters.description: True to have the comma character be the delimiter (DataType must be xlDelimited). The default value is False.

parameters.name: Space
parameters.description: True to have the space character be the delimiter (DataType must be xlDelimited). The default value is False.

parameters.name: Other
parameters.description: True to have the character specified by the _OtherChar_ argument be the delimiter (DataType must be xlDelimited). The default value is False.

parameters.name: OtherChar
parameters.description: Required if _Other_ is True. Specifies the delimiter character when _Other_ is True. If more than one character is specified, only the first character of the string is used; the remaining characters are ignored.

parameters.name: FieldInfo
parameters.description: An array containing parse information for individual columns of data. The interpretation depends on the value of _DataType_. When the data is delimited, this argument is an array of two-element arrays, with each two-element array specifying the conversion options for a particular column. The first element is the column number (1-based), and the second element is one of the XlColumnDataType constants specifying how the column is parsed.

parameters.name: TextVisualLayout
parameters.description: The visual layout of the text.

parameters.name: DecimalSeparator
parameters.description: The decimal separator that Microsoft Excel uses when recognizing numbers. The default setting is the system setting.

parameters.name: ThousandsSeparator
parameters.description: The thousands separator that Excel uses when recognizing numbers. The default setting is the system setting.

parameters.name: TrailingMinusNumbers
parameters.description: Specify True if numbers with a minus character at the end should be treated as negative numbers. If False or omitted, numbers with a minus character at the end are treated as text.

parameters.name: Local
parameters.description: Specify True if regional settings of the machine should be used for separators, numbers and data formatting.

methods.name: PivotTableWizard
methods.signature: PivotTableWizard([SourceType As Variant], [SourceData As Variant], [TableDestination As Variant], [TableName As Variant], [RowGrand As Variant], [ColumnGrand As Variant], [SaveData As Variant], [HasAutoFormat As Variant], [AutoPage As Variant], [Reserved As Variant], [BackgroundQuery As Variant], [OptimizeCache As Variant], [PageFieldOrder As Variant], [PageFieldWrapCount As Variant], [ReadData As Variant], [Connection As Variant]) As PivotTable
methods.description: Creates a new PivotTable report. This method doesn't display the PivotTable Wizard. This method isn't available for OLE DB data sources. Use the Add method to add a PivotTable cache, and then create a PivotTable report based on the cache.

parameters.name: SourceType
parameters.description: An XlPivotTableSourceType value that represents the source of the report data. If you specify this argument, you must also specify _SourceData_. If _SourceType_ and _SourceData_ are omitted, Microsoft Excel assumes that the source type is xlDatabase, and the source data comes from the named range Database. If this named range doesn't exist, Excel uses the current region if the current selection is in a range of more than 10 cells that contain data. If this isn't true, this method will fail.

parameters.name: SourceData
parameters.description: The data for the new report. Can be a Range object, an array of ranges, or a text constant that represents the name of another report. For an external database, _SourceData_ is an array of strings containing the SQL query string, where each element is up to 255 characters in length. You should use the _Connection_ argument to specify the ODBC connection string. For compatibility with earlier versions of Excel, _SourceData_ can be a two-element array. The first element is the connection string specifying the ODBC source for the data. The second element is the SQL query string used to get the data. If you specify _SourceData_, you must also specify _SourceType_. If the active cell is inside the _SourceData_ range, you must specify _TableDestination_ as well.

parameters.name: TableDestination
parameters.description: A Range object specifying where the report should be placed on the worksheet. If this argument is omitted, the report is placed at the active cell.

parameters.name: TableName
parameters.description: A string that specifies the name of the new report.

parameters.name: RowGrand
parameters.description: True to show grand totals for rows in the report.

parameters.name: ColumnGrand
parameters.description: True to show grand totals for columns in the report.

parameters.name: SaveData
parameters.description: True to save data with the report. False to save only the report definition.

parameters.name: HasAutoFormat
parameters.description: True to have Excel automatically format the report when it's refreshed or when fields are moved.

parameters.name: AutoPage
parameters.description: Valid only if _SourceType_ is xlConsolidation. True to have Excel create a page field for the consolidation. If _AutoPage_ is False, you must create the page field or fields.

parameters.name: Reserved
parameters.description: Not used by Excel.

parameters.name: BackgroundQuery
parameters.description: True to have Excel perform queries for the report asynchronously (in the background). The default value is False.

parameters.name: OptimizeCache
parameters.description: True to optimize the PivotTable cache when it's constructed. The default value is False.

parameters.name: PageFieldOrder
parameters.description: The order in which page fields are added to the PivotTable report's layout. Can be one of the following XlOrder constants: xlDownThenOver (default) or xlOverThenDown.

parameters.name: PageFieldWrapCount
parameters.description: The number of page fields in each column or row in the PivotTable report. The default value is 0 (zero).

parameters.name: ReadData
parameters.description: True to create a PivotTable cache that contains all records from the external database; this cache can be very large. If _ReadData_ is False, you can set some of the fields as server-based page fields before the data is actually read.

parameters.name: Connection
parameters.description: A string that contains ODBC settings that allow Excel to connect to an ODBC data source. The connection string has the form ODBC;<connection string>. This argument overrides any previous setting for the PivotCache object's Connection property.

methods.name: Protect
methods.signature: Protect([Password As Variant], [DrawingObjects As Variant], [Contents As Variant], [Scenarios As Variant], [UserInterfaceOnly As Variant], [AllowFormattingCells As Variant], [AllowFormattingColumns As Variant], [AllowFormattingRows As Variant], [AllowInsertingColumns As Variant], [AllowInsertingRows As Variant], [AllowInsertingHyperlinks As Variant], [AllowDeletingColumns As Variant], [AllowDeletingRows As Variant], [AllowSorting As Variant], [AllowFiltering As Variant], [AllowUsingPivotTables As Variant])
methods.description: Protects a worksheet so that it cannot be modified.

parameters.name: Password
parameters.description: A string that specifies a case-sensitive password for the worksheet or workbook. If this argument is omitted, you can unprotect the worksheet or workbook without using a password. Otherwise, you must specify the password to unprotect the worksheet or workbook. If you forget the password, you cannot unprotect the worksheet or workbook. Use strong passwords that combine uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols. Weak passwords don't mix these elements. Strong password: Y6dh!et5. Weak password: House27. Passwords should be 8 or more characters in length. A pass phrase that uses 14 or more characters is better. It's critical that you remember your password. If you forget your password, Microsoft cannot retrieve it. Store the passwords that you write down in a secure place away from the information that they help protect.

parameters.name: DrawingObjects
parameters.description: True to protect shapes. The default value is True.

parameters.name: Contents
parameters.description: True to protect contents. For a chart, this protects the entire chart. For a worksheet, this protects the locked cells. The default value is True.

parameters.name: Scenarios
parameters.description: True to protect scenarios. This argument is valid only for worksheets. The default value is True.

parameters.name: UserInterfaceOnly
parameters.description: True to protect the user interface, but not macros. If this argument is omitted, protection applies both to macros and to the user interface.

parameters.name: AllowFormattingCells
parameters.description: True allows the user to format any cell on a protected worksheet. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowFormattingColumns
parameters.description: True allows the user to format any column on a protected worksheet. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowFormattingRows
parameters.description: True allows the user to format any row on a protected worksheet. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowInsertingColumns
parameters.description: True allows the user to insert columns on the protected worksheet. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowInsertingRows
parameters.description: True allows the user to insert rows on the protected worksheet. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowInsertingHyperlinks
parameters.description: True allows the user to insert hyperlinks on the protected worksheet. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowDeletingColumns
parameters.description: True allows the user to delete columns on the protected worksheet, where every cell in the column to be deleted is unlocked. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowDeletingRows
parameters.description: True allows the user to delete rows on the protected worksheet, where every cell in the row to be deleted is unlocked. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowSorting
parameters.description: True allows the user to sort on the protected worksheet. Every cell in the sort range must be unlocked or unprotected. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowFiltering
parameters.description: True allows the user to set filters on the protected worksheet. Users can change filter criteria but can not enable or disable an auto filter. Users can set filters on an existing auto filter. The default value is False.

parameters.name: AllowUsingPivotTables
parameters.description: True allows the user to use PivotTable reports on the protected worksheet. The default value is False.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Lookup_value - A value that Lookup searches for in the first vector. Lookup_value can be a number, text, a logical value, or a name or reference that refers to a value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Lookup_vector or Array - In vector form, a range that contains only one row or one column. The values in lookup_vector can be text, numbers, or logical values. In array form, a range of cells that contains text, numbers, or logical values that you want to compare with lookup_value.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Result_vector - Only used with the vector form. A range that contains only one row or column. It must be the same size as lookup_vector.

parameters.description: Array or Reference - a range of cells or an array constant. For references, it is the reference to one or more cell ranges.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Row_num - selects the row in array from which to return a value. If row_num is omitted, column_num is required. For references, the number of the row in reference from which to return a reference.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Column_num - selects the column in array from which to return a value. If column_num is omitted, row_num is required. For reference, the number of the column in reference from which to return a reference.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Area_num - only used when returning references. Selects a range in reference from which to return the intersection of row_num and column_num. The first area selected or entered is numbered 1, the second is 2, and so on. If area_num is omitted, Index uses area 1.

methods.name: LinEst
methods.signature: LinEst(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Calculates the statistics for a line by using the least squares method to calculate a straight line that best fits your data, and returns an array that describes the line. Because this function returns an array of values, it must be entered as an array formula.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - the set of y-values that you already know in the relationship y = mx + b.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - an optional set of x-values that you may already know in the relationship y = mx + b.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Const - a logical value specifying whether to force the constant b to equal 0.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Stats - a logical value specifying whether to return additional regression statistics.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - the set of y-values that you already know in the relationship y = mx + b.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - an optional set of x-values that you may already know in the relationship y = mx + b.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: New_x's - new x-values for which you want Trend to return corresponding y-values.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Const - a logical value specifying whether to force the constant b to equal 0.

parameters.name: Arg2

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Const - a logical value specifying whether to force the constant b to equal 1.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Stats - a logical value specifying whether to return additional regression statistics.

methods.name: Pv
methods.signature: Pv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the present value of an investment. The present value is the total amount that a series of future payments is worth now. For example, when you borrow money, the loan amount is the present value to the lender.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate per period. For example, if you obtain an automobile loan at a 10 percent annual interest rate and make monthly payments, your interest rate per month is 10%/12, or 0.83%. You would enter 10%/12, or 0.83%, or 0.0083, into the formula as the rate.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods in an annuity. For example, if you get a four-year car loan and make monthly payments, your loan has 4*12 (or 48) periods. You would enter 48 into the formula for nper.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pmt - the payment made each period and cannot change over the life of the annuity. Typically, pmt includes principal and interest but no other fees or taxes. For example, the monthly payments on a $10,000, four-year car loan at 12 percent are $263.33. You would enter -263.33 into the formula as the pmt. If pmt is omitted, you must include the fv argument.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (the future value of a loan, for example, is 0). For example, if you want to save $50,000 to pay for a special project in 18 years, $50,000 is the future value. You could then make a conservative guess at an interest rate and determine how much you must save each month. If fv is omitted, you must include the pmt argument.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1; indicates when payments are due.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods in an annuity.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pmt - the payment made each period; it cannot change over the life of the annuity. Typically, pmt contains principal and interest but no other fees or taxes. If pmt is omitted, you must include the pv argument.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Pv - the present value, or the lump-sum amount that a series of future payments is worth right now. If pv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (zero), and you must include the pmt argument.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1 and indicates when payments are due. If type is omitted, it is assumed to be 0.

methods.name: NPer
methods.signature: NPer(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the number of periods for an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate per period.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Pmt - the payment made each period; it cannot change over the life of the annuity. Typically, pmt contains principal and interest but no other fees or taxes.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pv - the present value, or the lump-sum amount that a series of future payments is worth right now.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance that you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (the future value of a loan, for example, is 0).

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1 and indicates when payments are due.

methods.name: Pmt
methods.signature: Pmt(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the payment for a loan based on constant payments and a constant interest rate.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate for the loan.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payments for the loan.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pv - the present value, or the total amount that a series of future payments is worth now; also known as the principal.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (zero), that is, the future value of a loan is 0.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 (zero) or 1; indicates when payments are due.

methods.name: Rate
methods.signature: Rate(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the interest rate per period of an annuity. Rate is calculated by iteration and can have zero or more solutions. If the successive results of Rate don't converge to within 0.0000001 after 20 iterations, Rate returns the #NUM! error value.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods in an annuity.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Pmt - the payment made each period and cannot change over the life of the annuity. Typically, pmt includes principal and interest but no other fees or taxes. If pmt is omitted, you must include the fv argument.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Pv - the present value—the total amount that a series of future payments is worth now.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (the future value of a loan, for example, is 0).

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1; indicates when payments are due.

parameters.name: Arg6
parameters.description: Guess - your guess for what the rate will be.

methods.name: MIrr
methods.signature: MIrr(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the modified internal rate of return for a series of periodic cash flows. MIrr considers both the cost of the investment and the interest received on reinvestment of cash.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Values - an array or a reference to cells that contain numbers. These numbers represent a series of payments (negative values) and income (positive values) occurring at regular periods.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Finance_rate - the interest rate you pay on the money used in the cash flows.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Reinvest_rate - the interest rate you receive on the cash flows as you reinvest them.

methods.name: Irr
methods.signature: Irr(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the internal rate of return for a series of cash flows represented by the numbers in values. These cash flows don't have to be even, as they would be for an annuity. However, the cash flows must occur at regular intervals, such as monthly or annually. The internal rate of return is the interest rate received for an investment consisting of payments (negative values) and income (positive values) that occur at regular periods.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Values - an array or a reference to cells that contain numbers for which you want to calculate the internal rate of return.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Guess - a number that you guess is close to the result of Irr.

methods.name: Match
methods.signature: Match(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the relative position of an item in an array that matches a specified value in a specified order. Use Match instead of one of the Lookup functions when you need the position of an item in a range instead of the item itself.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Lookup_value: the value that you use to find the value that you want in a table.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Lookup_array: a contiguous range of cells containing possible lookup values. Lookup_array must be an array or an array reference.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Match_type: the number -1, 0, or 1. Match_type specifies how Microsoft Excel matches lookup_value with values in lookup_array.

methods.name: Weekday
methods.signature: Weekday(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the day of the week corresponding to a date. The day is given as an integer, ranging from 1 (Sunday) to 7 (Saturday), by default.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Serial_number - a sequential number that represents the date of the day you are trying to find. Dates should be entered by using the DATE function, or as results of other formulas or functions. For example, use DATE(2008,5,23) for the 23rd day of May, 2008. Problems can occur if dates are entered as text.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Return_type - a number that determines the type of return value.

methods.name: Search
methods.signature: Search(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Search and SearchB locate one text string within a second text string, and return the number of the starting position of the first text string from the first character of the second text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Find_text - the text that you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Within_text - the text in which you want to search for find_text.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Start_num - the character number in within_text at which you want to start searching.

methods.name: Transpose
methods.description: Returns a vertical range of cells as a horizontal range, or vice versa. Transpose must be entered as an array formula in a range that has the same number of rows and columns, respectively, as an array has columns and rows. Use Transpose to shift the vertical and horizontal orientation of an array on a worksheet.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - an array or range of cells on a worksheet that you want to transpose. The transpose of an array is created by using the first row of the array as the first column of the new array, the second row of the array as the second column of the new array, and so on.

methods.name: Atan2
methods.signature: Atan2(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the arctangent, or inverse tangent, of the specified x- and y-coordinates. The arctangent is the angle from the x-axis to a line containing the origin (0, 0) and a point with coordinates (x_num, y_num). The angle is given in radians between -pi and pi, excluding -pi.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the point.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the point.

methods.name: Asin
methods.description: Returns the arcsine, or inverse sine, of a number. The arcsine is the angle whose sine is _Arg1_. The returned angle is given in radians in the range -pi/2 to pi/2.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The sine of the angle that you want; must be from -1 to 1.

methods.name: Acos
methods.description: Returns the arccosine, or inverse cosine, of a number. The arccosine is the angle whose cosine is _Arg1_. The returned angle is given in radians in the range 0 (zero) to pi.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The cosine of the angle you want, and must be from -1 to 1.

methods.name: Choose
methods.signature: Choose(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Uses _Arg1_ as the index to return a value from the list of value arguments.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Specifies which value argument is selected. _Arg1_ must be a number between 1 and 29, or a formula or reference to a cell containing a number between 1 and 29.

methods.name: HLookup
methods.signature: HLookup(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant, [Arg4 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Searches for a value in the top row of a table or an array of values, and then returns a value in the same column from a row that you specify in the table or array. Use HLookup when your comparison values are located in a row across the top of a table of data, and you want to look down a specified number of rows. Use VLookup when your comparison values are located in a column to the left of the data that you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Lookup_value - the value to be found in the first row of the table. Lookup_value can be a value, a reference, or a text string.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Table_array - a table of information in which data is looked up. Use a reference to a range or a range name.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Row_index_num - the row number in table_array from which the matching value will be returned. A row_index_num of 1 returns the first row value in table_array, a row_index_num of 2 returns the second row value in table_array, and so on. If row_index_num is less than 1, HLookup returns the #VALUE! error value; if row_index_num is greater than the number of rows on table_array, HLookup returns the #REF! error value.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Range_lookup - a logical value that specifies whether you want HLookup to find an exact match or an approximate match. If True or omitted, an approximate match is returned. In other words, if an exact match is not found, the next largest value that is less than lookup_value is returned. If False, HLookup will find an exact match. If one is not found, the error value #N/A is returned.

methods.name: VLookup
methods.signature: VLookup(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant, [Arg4 As Variant]) As Variant
methods.description: Searches for a value in the first column of a table array and returns a value in the same row from another column in the table array.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Lookup_value - the value to search in the first column of the table array. Lookup_value can be a value or a reference. If lookup_value is smaller than the smallest value in the first column of table_array, VLookup returns the #N/A error value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Table_array - two or more columns of data. Use a reference to a range or a range name. The values in the first column of table_array are the values searched by lookup_value. These values can be text, numbers, or logical values. Uppercase and lowercase text are equivalent.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Col_index_num - the column number in table_array from which the matching value must be returned. A col_index_num of 1 returns the value in the first column in table_array; a col_index_num of 2 returns the value in the second column in table_array, and so on.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Range_lookup - a logical value that specifies whether you want the VLookup method to find an exact match or an approximate match.

methods.name: Log
methods.signature: Log(Arg1 As Double, [Arg2 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the logarithm of a number to the base that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the positive real number for which you want the logarithm.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Base - the base of the logarithm. If base is omitted, it is assumed to be 10.

methods.name: Proper
methods.description: Capitalizes the first letter in a text string and any other letters in text that follow any character other than a letter. Converts all other letters to lowercase letters.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text - text enclosed in quotation marks, a formula that returns text, or a reference to a cell containing the text that you want to partially capitalize.

methods.name: Trim
methods.description: Removes all spaces from text except for single spaces between words. Use Trim on text that you have received from another application that may have irregular spacing.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text - the text from which you want spaces removed.

methods.name: Replace
methods.signature: Replace(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As String) As String
methods.description: Replaces part of a text string, based on the number of characters that you specify, with a different text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text in which you want to replace some characters.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The position of the character in _Arg1_ that you want to replace with _Arg4_.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The number of characters in _Arg1_ that you want the Replace method to replace with _Arg4_.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Text that will replace characters in _Arg1_.

methods.name: Substitute
methods.signature: Substitute(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, Arg3 As String, [Arg4 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Substitutes new_text for old_text in a text string. Use Substitute when you want to replace specific text in a text string; use Replace when you want to replace any text that occurs in a specific location in a text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Text - the text or the reference to a cell containing text for which you want to substitute characters.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Old_text - the text that you want to replace.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: New_text - the text that you want to replace old_text with.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Instance_num - specifies which occurrence of old_text you want to replace with new_text. If you specify instance_num, only that instance of old_text is replaced. Otherwise, every occurrence of old_text in text is changed to new_text.

methods.name: Find
methods.signature: Find(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Finds specific information on a worksheet.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The name of the worksheet.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The name of the range.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The name of an argument to refine the search.

methods.name: IsErr
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to any error value except #N/A.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: IsText
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to text.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: IsNumber
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to a number.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: Sln
methods.signature: Sln(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the straight-line depreciation of an asset for one period.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

methods.name: Syd
methods.signature: Syd(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum-of-years' digits depreciation of an asset for a specified period.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Per - the period and must use the same units as life.

methods.name: Ddb
methods.signature: Ddb(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset for a specified period by using the double-declining balance method or some other method that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset). This value can be 0.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is being depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Period - the period for which you want to calculate the depreciation. Period must use the same units as life.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Factor - the rate at which the balance declines. If factor is omitted, it is assumed to be 2 (the double-declining balance method).

methods.name: Clean
methods.description: Removes all nonprintable characters from text.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Any worksheet information from which you want to remove nonprintable characters.

methods.name: MDeterm
methods.description: Returns the matrix determinant of an array.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - a numeric array with an equal number of rows and columns.

methods.name: MInverse
methods.description: Returns the inverse matrix for the matrix stored in an array.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - a numeric array with an equal number of rows and columns.

methods.name: MMult
methods.signature: MMult(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Variant
methods.description: Returns the matrix product of two arrays. The result is an array with the same number of rows as array1 and the same number of columns as array2.

methods.name: Ipmt
methods.signature: Ipmt(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the interest payment for a given period for an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate per period.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Per - the period for which you want to find the interest; must be in the range 1 to nper.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods in an annuity.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Pv - the present value, or the lump-sum amount that a series of future payments is worth right now.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance that you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (the future value of a loan, for example, is 0).

parameters.name: Arg6
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1 and indicates when payments are due. If type is omitted, it is assumed to be 0.

methods.name: Ppmt
methods.signature: Ppmt(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the payment on the principal for a given period for an investment based on periodic, constant payments and a constant interest rate.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate per period.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Per - the period and must be in the range 1 to nper.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods in an annuity.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Pv - the present value—the total amount that a series of future payments is worth now.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Fv - the future value, or a cash balance you want to attain after the last payment is made. If fv is omitted, it is assumed to be 0 (zero), that is, the future value of a loan is 0.

parameters.name: Arg6
parameters.description: Type - the number 0 or 1 and indicates when payments are due.

methods.name: CountA
methods.signature: CountA(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Counts the number of cells that are not empty and the values within the list of arguments.

methods.name: Product
methods.signature: Product(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Multiplies all the numbers given as arguments and returns the product.

methods.name: Fact
methods.description: Returns the factorial of a number. The factorial of a number is equal to 1\2\3\...\ number.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the nonnegative number that you want the factorial of. If number is not an integer, it is truncated.

methods.name: DProduct
methods.signature: DProduct(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Multiplies the values in a column of a list or database that match conditions that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Database is the range of cells that makes up the list or database. A database is a list of related data in which rows of related information are records, and columns of data are fields. The first row of the list contains labels for each column.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Field indicates which column is used in the function. Enter the column label enclosed between double quotation marks, such as "Age" or "Yield," or a number (without quotation marks) that represents the position of the column within the list: 1 for the first column, 2 for the second column, and so on.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Criteria is the range of cells that contains the conditions that you specify. Use any range for the criteria argument, as long as it includes at least one column label and at least one cell below the column label in which you specify a condition for the column.

methods.name: IsNonText
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to any item that is not text. (Note that this function returns True if value refers to a blank cell.)

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: StDevP
methods.signature: StDevP(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Calculates standard deviation based on the entire population given as arguments. The standard deviation is a measure of how widely values are dispersed from the average value (the mean).

methods.name: VarP
methods.signature: VarP(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Calculates variance based on the entire population.

methods.name: DStDevP
methods.signature: DStDevP(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the standard deviation of a population based on the entire population by using the numbers in a column of a list or database that match conditions that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Database - is the range of cells that makes up the list or database. A database is a list of related data in which rows of related information are records, and columns of data are fields. The first row of the list contains labels for each column.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Field - indicates which column is used in the function. Enter the column label enclosed between double quotation marks, such as "Age" or "Yield," or a number (without quotation marks) that represents the position of the column within the list: 1 for the first column, 2 for the second column, and so on.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Criteria - the range of cells that contains the conditions that you specify. Use any range for the criteria argument, as long as it includes at least one column label and at least one cell below the column label in which you specify a condition for the column.

methods.name: DVarP
methods.signature: DVarP(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the variance of a population based on the entire population by using the numbers in a column of a list or database that match conditions that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Database - the range of cells that makes up the list or database. A database is a list of related data in which rows of related information are records, and columns of data are fields. The first row of the list contains labels for each column.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Field - indicates which column is used in the function. Enter the column label enclosed between double quotation marks, such as "Age" or "Yield," or a number (without quotation marks) that represents the position of the column within the list: 1 for the first column, 2 for the second column, and so on.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Criteria - the range of cells that contains the conditions that you specify. Use any range for the criteria argument, as long as it includes at least one column label and at least one cell below the column label in which you specify a condition for the column.

methods.name: IsLogical
methods.description: Checks the type of value and returns True or False depending on whether the value refers to a logical value.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Value - the value that you want tested. Value can be a blank (empty cell), error, logical, text, number, or reference value, or a name referring to any of these, that you want to test.

methods.name: DCountA
methods.signature: DCountA(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Counts the nonblank cells in a column of a list or database that match conditions that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Database - the range of cells that makes up the list or database. A database is a list of related data in which rows of related information are records, and columns of data are fields. The first row of the list contains labels for each column.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Field - indicates which column is used in the function. Enter the column label enclosed between double quotation marks, such as "Age" or "Yield," or a number (without quotation marks) that represents the position of the column within the list: 1 for the first column, 2 for the second column, and so on.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Criteria - the range of cells that contains the conditions that you specify. Use any range for the criteria argument, as long as it includes at least one column label and at least one cell below the column label in which you specify a condition for the column.

methods.name: USDollar
methods.signature: USDollar(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As String
methods.description: Converts a number to text format and applies a currency symbol. The name of the method (and the symbol that it applies) depends upon the language settings.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A reference to a cell containing a number, or a formula that evaluates to a number.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The number of digits to the right of the decimal point. If _Arg2_ is negative, the number is rounded to the left of the decimal point. If you omit decimals, it is assumed to be 2.

methods.name: FindB
methods.signature: FindB(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Find and FindB locate one text string within a second text string, and return the number of the starting position of the first text string from the first character of the second text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Find_text - the text you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Within_text - the text containing the text that you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Start_num - specifies the character at which to start the search. The first character in within_text is character number 1. If you omit start_num, it is assumed to be 1.

methods.name: SearchB
methods.signature: SearchB(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As String, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Search and SearchB locate one text string within a second text string, and return the number of the starting position of the first text string from the first character of the second text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Find_text - the text that you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Within_text - the text in which you want to search for find_text.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Start_num - the character number in within_text at which you want to start searching.

methods.name: ReplaceB
methods.signature: ReplaceB(Arg1 As String, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As String) As String
methods.description: Replaces part of a text string, based on the number of bytes that you specify, with a different text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Old_text - text in which you want to replace some characters.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Start_num - the position of the character in old_text that you want to replace with new_text.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Num_chars - the number of characters in old_text that you want Replace to replace with new_text.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: New_text - the text that will replace characters in old_text.

methods.name: RoundUp
methods.signature: RoundUp(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Rounds a number up, away from 0 (zero).

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - any real number that you want rounded up.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Num_digits - the number of digits to which you want to round number.

methods.name: RoundDown
methods.signature: RoundDown(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Rounds a number down, toward 0 (zero).

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - any real number that you want rounded down.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Num_digits - the number of digits to which you want to round number.

methods.name: Rank
methods.signature: Rank(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Range, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the rank of a number in a list of numbers. The rank of a number is its size relative to other values in a list. If you were to sort the list, the rank of the number would be its position.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the number whose rank you want to find.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Ref - an array of, or a reference to, a list of numbers. Nonnumeric values in ref are ignored.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Order - a number specifying how to rank number.

methods.name: Days360
methods.signature: Days360(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the number of days between two dates based on a 360-day year (twelve 30-day months), which is used in some accounting calculations.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: A Boolean value that specifies whether to use the U.S. or European method in the calculation.

methods.name: Vdb
methods.signature: Vdb(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, Arg5 As Double, [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset for any period that you specify, including partial periods, by using the double-declining balance method or some other method that you specify. Vdb stands for variable declining balance.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset). This value can be 0.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Start_period - the starting period for which you want to calculate the depreciation. Start_period must use the same units as life.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: End_period - the ending period for which you want to calculate the depreciation. End_period must use the same units as life.

parameters.name: Arg6
parameters.description: Factor - the rate at which the balance declines. If factor is omitted, it is assumed to be 2 (the double-declining balance method). Change factor if you don't want to use the double-declining balance method. For a description of the double-declining balance method, see Ddb.

parameters.name: Arg7
parameters.description: No_switch - a logical value specifying whether to switch to straight-line depreciation when depreciation is greater than the declining balance calculation.

methods.name: Median
methods.signature: Median(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the median of the given numbers. The median is the number in the middle of a set of numbers.

methods.name: SumProduct
methods.signature: SumProduct(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Multiplies corresponding components in the given arrays, and returns the sum of those products.

methods.name: Sinh
methods.description: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a number.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number is any real number.

methods.name: Cosh
methods.description: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Any real number for which you want to find the hyperbolic cosine.

methods.name: Tanh
methods.description: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a number.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - any real number.

methods.name: Asinh
methods.description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of a number. The inverse hyperbolic sine is the value whose hyperbolic sine is _Arg1_, so Asinh(Sinh(number)) equals _Arg1_.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Any real number.

methods.name: Acosh
methods.description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of a number. Number must be greater than or equal to 1. The inverse hyperbolic cosine is the value whose hyperbolic cosine is _Arg1_, so Acosh(Cosh(number)) equals _Arg1_.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Any real number equal to or greater than 1.

methods.name: Atanh
methods.description: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of a number. Number must be between -1 and 1 (excluding -1 and 1).

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Any real number between 1 and -1.

methods.name: DGet
methods.signature: DGet(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Variant) As Variant
methods.description: Extracts a single value from a column of a list or database that matches conditions that you specify.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Database - the range of cells that makes up the list or database. A database is a list of related data in which rows of related information are records, and columns of data are fields. The first row of the list contains labels for each column.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Field - indicates which column is used in the function. Enter the column label enclosed between double quotation marks, such as "Age" or "Yield," or a number (without quotation marks) that represents the position of the column within the list: 1 for the first column, 2 for the second column, and so on.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Criteria - the range of cells that contains the conditions that you specify. Use any range for the criteria argument, as long as it includes at least one column label and at least one cell below the column label in which you specify a condition for the column.

methods.name: Db
methods.signature: Db(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the depreciation of an asset for a specified period using the fixed-declining balance method.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Cost - the initial cost of the asset.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Salvage - the value at the end of the depreciation (sometimes called the salvage value of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Life - the number of periods over which the asset is being depreciated (sometimes called the useful life of the asset).

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Period - the period for which you want to calculate the depreciation. Period must use the same units as life.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Month - the number of months in the first year. If month is omitted, it is assumed to be 12.

methods.name: Frequency
methods.signature: Frequency(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Variant
methods.description: Calculates how often values occur within a range of values, and then returns a vertical array of numbers. For example, use Frequency to count the number of test scores that fall within ranges of scores. Because Frequency returns an array, it must be entered as an array formula.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Data_array - an array of or reference to a set of values for which you want to count frequencies. If data_array contains no values, Frequency returns an array of zeros.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Bins_array - an array of or reference to intervals into which you want to group the values in data_array. If bins_array contains no values, Frequency returns the number of elements in data_array.

methods.name: AveDev
methods.signature: AveDev(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the average of the absolute deviations of data points from their mean. AveDev is a measure of the variability in a data set.

methods.name: BetaDist
methods.signature: BetaDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the beta cumulative distribution function.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The value between A and B at which to evaluate the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: A parameter of the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: A parameter of the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: An optional lower bound to the interval of x.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: An optional upper bound to the interval of x.

methods.name: GammaLn
methods.description: Returns the natural logarithm of the gamma function, (x).

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value for which you want to calculate GammaLn.

methods.name: BetaInv
methods.signature: BetaInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the inverse of the cumulative distribution function for a specified beta distribution. That is, if probability = BetaDist(x,...), then BetaInv(probability,...) = x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A probability associated with the beta distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The Alpha parameter of the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The Beta parameter the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: An optional lower bound to the interval of x.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: An optional upper bound to the interval of x.

methods.name: BinomDist
methods.signature: BinomDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the individual term binomial distribution probability.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The number of successes in trials.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The number of independent trials.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The probability of success on each trial.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: A logical value that determines the form of the function. If cumulative is True, BinomDist returns the cumulative distribution function, which is the probability that there are at most number_s successes; if False, it returns the probability mass function, which is the probability that there are number_s successes.

methods.name: ChiDist
methods.signature: ChiDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the one-tailed probability of the chi-squared distribution.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The value at which you want to evaluate the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The number of degrees of freedom.

methods.name: ChiInv
methods.signature: ChiInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the inverse of the one-tailed probability of the chi-squared distribution.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A probability associated with the chi-squared distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The number of degrees of freedom.

methods.name: Combin
methods.signature: Combin(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the number of combinations for a given number of items. Use Combin to determine the total possible number of groups for a given number of items.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The number of items.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The number of items in each combination.

methods.name: Confidence
methods.signature: Confidence(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns a value that you can use to construct a confidence interval for a population mean.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The significance level used to compute the confidence level. The confidence level equals 100*(1 - alpha)%, or in other words, an alpha of 0.05 indicates a 95 percent confidence level.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The population standard deviation for the data range; is assumed to be known.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The sample size.

methods.name: CritBinom
methods.signature: CritBinom(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the smallest value for which the cumulative binomial distribution is greater than or equal to a criterion value.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The number of Bernoulli trials.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The probability of a success on each trial.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: The criterion value.

methods.name: Even
methods.description: Returns number rounded up to the nearest even integer. Use this function for processing items that come in twos. For example, a packing crate accepts rows of one or two items. The crate is full when the number of items, rounded up to the nearest two, matches the crate's capacity.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the value to round.

methods.name: ExponDist
methods.signature: ExponDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the exponential distribution. Use ExponDist to model the time between events, such as how long an automated bank teller takes to deliver cash. For example, you can use ExponDist to determine the probability that the process takes at most 1 minute.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value of the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Lambda - the parameter value.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Cumulative - a logical value that indicates which form of the exponential function to provide. If cumulative is True, ExponDist returns the cumulative distribution function; if False, it returns the probability density function.

methods.name: FDist
methods.signature: FDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the F probability distribution. Use this function to determine whether two data sets have different degrees of diversity. For example, you can examine the test scores of men and women entering high school and determine if the variability in the females is different from that found in the males.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value at which to evaluate the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom1 - the numerator degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom2 - the denominator degrees of freedom.

methods.name: FInv
methods.signature: FInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the inverse of the F probability distribution. If p = FDIST(x,...), then FINV(p,...) = x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Probability - a probability associated with the F cumulative distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom1 - the numerator degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom2 - is the denominator degrees of freedom.

methods.name: Fisher
methods.description: Returns the Fisher transformation at x. This transformation produces a function that is normally distributed rather than skewed. Use this function to perform hypothesis testing on the correlation coefficient.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: x - a numeric value for which you want the transformation.

methods.name: FisherInv
methods.description: Returns the inverse of the Fisher transformation. Use this transformation when analyzing correlations between ranges or arrays of data. If y = FISHER(x), then FISHERINV(y) = x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: y - the value for which you want to perform the inverse of the transformation.

methods.name: Floor
methods.signature: Floor(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Rounds number down, toward zero, to the nearest multiple of significance.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the numeric value that you want to round.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Significance - the multiple to which you want to round.

methods.name: GammaDist
methods.signature: GammaDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the gamma distribution. Use this function to study variables that may have a skewed distribution. The gamma distribution is commonly used in queuing analysis.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value at which you want to evaluate the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Alpha - a parameter to the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Beta - a parameter to the distribution. If beta = 1, GammaDist returns the standard gamma distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Cumulative - a logical value that determines the form of the function. If cumulative is True, GammaDist returns the cumulative distribution function; if False, it returns the probability density function.

methods.name: GammaInv
methods.signature: GammaInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the inverse of the gamma cumulative distribution. If p = GAMMADIST(x,...), then GAMMAINV(p,...) = x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Probability - the probability associated with the gamma distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Alpha - a parameter to the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Beta - a parameter to the distribution. If beta = 1, GammaInv returns the standard gamma distribution.

methods.name: Ceiling
methods.signature: Ceiling(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns number rounded up, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of significance.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the value that you want to round.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Significance - the multiple to which you want to round.

methods.name: HypGeomDist
methods.signature: HypGeomDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the hypergeometric distribution.
