HypGeomDist returns the probability of a given number of sample successes, given the sample size, population successes, and population size. Use HypGeomDist for problems with a finite population, where each observation is either a success or a failure, and where each subset of a given size is chosen with equal likelihood.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Sample_s - the number of successes in the sample.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Number_sample - the size of the sample.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Population_s - the number of successes in the population.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Number_population - the population size.

methods.name: LogNormDist
methods.signature: LogNormDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the cumulative lognormal distribution of x, where ln(x) is normally distributed with parameters mean and standard_dev. Use this function to analyze data that has been logarithmically transformed.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value at which to evaluate the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Mean - the mean of ln(x).

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Standard_dev - the standard deviation of ln(x).

methods.name: LogInv
methods.signature: LogInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Use the lognormal distribution to analyze logarithmically transformed data.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Probability - a probability associated with the lognormal distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Mean - the mean of ln(x).

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Standard_dev - the standard deviation of ln(x).

methods.name: NegBinomDist
methods.signature: NegBinomDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the negative binomial distribution. NegBinomDist returns the probability that there will be number_f failures before the number_s-th success, when the constant probability of a success is probability_s. This function is similar to the binomial distribution, except that the number of successes is fixed, and the number of trials is variable. Like the binomial, trials are assumed to be independent.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number_f - the number of failures.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Number_s - the threshold number of successes.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Probability_s - the probability of a success.

methods.name: NormDist
methods.signature: NormDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the normal distribution for the specified mean and standard deviation. This function has a very wide range of applications in statistics, including hypothesis testing.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value for which you want the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Mean - the arithmetic mean of the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Standard_dev - the standard deviation of the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Cumulative - a logical value that determines the form of the function. If cumulative is True, NormDist returns the cumulative distribution function; if False, it returns the probability mass function.

methods.name: NormSDist
methods.description: Returns the standard normal cumulative distribution function. The distribution has a mean of 0 (zero) and a standard deviation of one. Use this function in place of a table of standard normal curve areas.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Z - the value for which you want the distribution.

methods.name: NormInv
methods.signature: NormInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the inverse of the normal cumulative distribution for the specified mean and standard deviation.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Probability - a probability corresponding to the normal distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Mean - the arithmetic mean of the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Standard_dev - the standard deviation of the distribution.

methods.name: NormSInv
methods.description: Returns the inverse of the standard normal cumulative distribution. The distribution has a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Probability - a probability corresponding to the normal distribution.

methods.name: Standardize
methods.signature: Standardize(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns a normalized value from a distribution characterized by mean and standard_dev.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value that you want to normalize.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Mean - the arithmetic mean of the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Standard_dev - the standard deviation of the distribution.

methods.name: Odd
methods.description: Returns number rounded up to the nearest odd integer.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the value to round.

methods.name: Permut
methods.signature: Permut(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the number of permutations for a given number of objects that can be selected from number objects. A permutation is any set or subset of objects or events where internal order is significant. Permutations are different from combinations, for which the internal order is not significant. Use this function for lottery-style probability calculations.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - an integer that describes the number of objects.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Number_chosen - an integer that describes the number of objects in each permutation.

methods.name: Poisson
methods.signature: Poisson(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Poisson distribution. A common application of the Poisson distribution is predicting the number of events over a specific time, such as the number of cars arriving at a toll plaza in 1 minute.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the number of events.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Mean - the expected numeric value.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Cumulative - a logical value that determines the form of the probability distribution returned. If cumulative is True, Poisson returns the cumulative Poisson probability that the number of random events occurring will be between zero and x inclusive; if False, it returns the Poisson probability mass function that the number of events occurring will be exactly x.

methods.name: TDist
methods.signature: TDist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Percentage Points (probability) for the Student t-distribution where a numeric value (x) is a calculated value of t for which the Percentage Points are to be computed. The t-distribution is used in the hypothesis testing of small sample data sets. Use this function in place of a table of critical values for the t-distribution.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the numeric value at which to evaluate the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom - an integer indicating the number of degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Tails - specifies the number of distribution tails to return. If tails = 1, TDist returns the one-tailed distribution. If tails = 2, TDist returns the two-tailed distribution.

methods.name: Weibull
methods.signature: Weibull(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Weibull distribution. Use this distribution in reliability analysis, such as calculating a device's mean time to failure.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X - the value at which to evaluate the function.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Alpha - a parameter to the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Beta - a parameter to the distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Cumulative - determines the form of the function.

methods.name: SumXMY2
methods.signature: SumXMY2(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of squares of differences of corresponding values in two arrays.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array_x - the first array or range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array_y - the second array or range of values.

methods.name: SumX2MY2
methods.signature: SumX2MY2(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of the difference of squares of corresponding values in two arrays.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array_x - the first array or range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array_y - the second array or range of values.

methods.name: SumX2PY2
methods.signature: SumX2PY2(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of the sum of squares of corresponding values in two arrays. The sum of the sum of squares is a common term in many statistical calculations.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array_x - the first array or range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array_y - the second array or range of values.

methods.name: ChiTest
methods.signature: ChiTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the test for independence.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The range of data that contains observations to test against expected values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The range of data that contains the ratio of the product of row totals and column totals to the grand total.

methods.name: Correl
methods.signature: Correl(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the correlation coefficient of the _Arg1_ and _Arg2_ cell ranges.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A cell range of values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: A second cell range of values.

methods.name: Covar
methods.signature: Covar(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns covariance, the average of the products of deviations for each data point pair.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The first cell range of integers.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The second cell range of integers.

methods.name: FTest
methods.signature: FTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the result of an F-test. An F-test returns the two-tailed probability that the variances in array1 and array2 are not significantly different. Use this function to determine whether two samples have different variances. For example, given test scores from public and private schools, you can test whether these schools have different levels of test score diversity.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array1 - the first array or range of data.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array2 - the second array or range of data.

methods.name: Intercept
methods.signature: Intercept(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the point at which a line will intersect the y-axis by using existing x-values and y-values. The intercept point is based on a best-fit regression line plotted through the known x-values and known y-values.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - the dependent set of observations or data.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - the independent set of observations or data.

methods.name: Pearson
methods.signature: Pearson(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient, r, a dimensionless index that ranges from -1.0 to 1.0 inclusive and reflects the extent of a linear relationship between two data sets.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array1 - a set of independent values.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array2 - a set of dependent values.

methods.name: RSq
methods.signature: RSq(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the square of the Pearson product moment correlation coefficient through data points in known_y's and known_x's. For more information, see Pearson. The r-squared value can be interpreted as the proportion of the variance in y attributable to the variance in x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - an array or range of data points.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - an array or range of data points.

methods.name: StEyx
methods.signature: StEyx(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the standard error of the predicted y-value for each x in the regression. The standard error is a measure of the amount of error in the prediction of y for an individual x.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - an array or range of dependent data points.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - an array or range of independent data points.

methods.name: Slope
methods.signature: Slope(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Returns the slope of the linear regression line through data points in known_y's and known_x's. The slope is the vertical distance divided by the horizontal distance between any two points on the line, which is the rate of change along the regression line.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Known_y's - an array or cell range of numeric dependent data points.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Known_x's - the set of independent data points.

methods.name: TTest
methods.signature: TTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the probability associated with a Student's t-Test. Use TTest to determine whether two samples are likely to have come from the same two underlying populations that have the same mean.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array1 - the first data set.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Array2 - the second data set.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Tails - specifies the number of distribution tails. If tails = 1, TTest uses the one-tailed distribution. If tails = 2, TTest uses the two-tailed distribution.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Type - the kind of t-Test to perform.

methods.name: Prob
methods.signature: Prob(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Variant, Arg3 As Double, [Arg4 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the probability that values in a range are between two limits. If upper_limit is not supplied, returns the probability that values in x_range are equal to lower_limit.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: X_range - the range of numeric values of x with which there are associated probabilities.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Prob_range - a set of probabilities associated with values in x_range.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Lower_limit - the lower bound on the value for which you want a probability.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Upper_limit - the optional upper bound on the value for which you want a probability.

methods.name: DevSq
methods.signature: DevSq(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of squares of deviations of data points from their sample mean.

methods.name: GeoMean
methods.signature: GeoMean(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the geometric mean of an array or range of positive data. For example, you can use GeoMean to calculate average growth rate given compound interest with variable rates.

methods.name: HarMean
methods.signature: HarMean(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the harmonic mean of a data set. The harmonic mean is the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of reciprocals.

methods.name: SumSq
methods.signature: SumSq(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the sum of the squares of the arguments.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number1, number2... - 1 to 30 arguments for which you want the sum of the squares. You can also use a single array or a reference to an array instead of arguments separated by commas.

methods.name: Kurt
methods.signature: Kurt(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the kurtosis of a data set. Kurtosis characterizes the relative peakedness or flatness of a distribution compared with the normal distribution. Positive kurtosis indicates a relatively peaked distribution. Negative kurtosis indicates a relatively flat distribution.

methods.name: Skew
methods.signature: Skew(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the skewness of a distribution. Skewness characterizes the degree of asymmetry of a distribution around its mean.

methods.name: ZTest
methods.signature: ZTest(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the one-tailed probability-value of a z-test. For a given hypothesized population mean, ZTest returns the probability that the sample mean would be greater than the average of observations in the data set (_array_); that is, the observed sample mean.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: _Array_ is the array or range of data against which to test the hypothesized population mean.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The value to test.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: _Sigma_ is the population (known) standard deviation. If omitted, the sample standard deviation is used.

methods.name: Large
methods.signature: Large(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the k-th largest value in a data set. Use this function to select a value based on its relative standing. For example, you can use Large to return the highest, runner-up, or third-place score.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of data for which you want to determine the k-th largest value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: K - the position (from the largest) in the array or cell range of data to return.

methods.name: Small
methods.signature: Small(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the k-th smallest value in a data set. Use this function to return values with a particular relative standing in a data set.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - an array or range of numerical data for which you want to determine the k-th smallest value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: K - the position (from the smallest) in the array or range of data to return.

methods.name: Quartile
methods.signature: Quartile(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the quartile of a data set. Quartiles often are used in sales and survey data to divide populations into groups. For example, you can use Quartile to find the top 25 percent of incomes in a population.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or cell range of numeric values for which you want the quartile value.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Quart - indicates which value to return.

methods.name: Percentile
methods.signature: Percentile(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the k-th percentile of values in a range. Use this function to establish a threshold of acceptance. For example, you can decide to examine candidates who score above the 90th percentile.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of data that defines relative standing.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: K - the percentile value in the range 0..1, inclusive.

methods.name: PercentRank
methods.signature: PercentRank(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the rank of a value in a data set as a percentage of the data set. This function can be used to evaluate the relative standing of a value within a data set. For example, you can use PercentRank to evaluate the standing of an aptitude test score among all scores for the test.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of data with numeric values that defines relative standing.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: X - the value for which you want to know the rank.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Significance - an optional value that identifies the number of significant digits for the returned percentage value. If omitted, PercentRank uses three digits (0.xxx).

methods.name: Mode
methods.signature: Mode(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant], [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Returns the most frequently occurring, or repetitive, value in an array or range of data.

methods.name: TrimMean
methods.signature: TrimMean(Arg1 As Variant, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the mean of the interior of a data set. TrimMean calculates the mean taken by excluding a percentage of data points from the top and bottom tails of a data set. Use this function when you wish to exclude outlying data from your analysis.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Array - the array or range of values to trim and average.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Percent - the fractional number of data points to exclude from the calculation. For example, if percent = 0.2, 4 points are trimmed from a data set of 20 points (20 x 0.2): 2 from the top and 2 from the bottom of the set.

methods.name: TInv
methods.signature: TInv(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the t-value of the Student's t-distribution as a function of the probability and the degrees of freedom.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Probability - the probability associated with the two-tailed Student's t-distribution.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Degrees_freedom - the number of degrees of freedom with which to characterize the distribution.

methods.name: Power
methods.signature: Power(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Returns the result of a number raised to a power.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the base number. It can be any real number.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Power - the exponent to which the base number is raised.

methods.name: Radians
methods.description: Converts degrees to radians.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Angle - an angle in degrees that you want to convert.

methods.name: Degrees
methods.description: Converts radians into degrees.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Angle - the angle in radians that you want to convert.

methods.name: Subtotal
methods.signature: Subtotal(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Range, [Arg3 As Variant], [Arg4 As Variant], [Arg5 As Variant], [Arg6 As Variant], [Arg7 As Variant], [Arg8 As Variant], [Arg9 As Variant], [Arg10 As Variant], [Arg11 As Variant], [Arg12 As Variant], [Arg13 As Variant], [Arg14 As Variant], [Arg15 As Variant], [Arg16 As Variant], [Arg17 As Variant], [Arg18 As Variant], [Arg19 As Variant], [Arg20 As Variant], [Arg21 As Variant], [Arg22 As Variant], [Arg23 As Variant], [Arg24 As Variant], [Arg25 As Variant], [Arg26 As Variant], [Arg27 As Variant], [Arg28 As Variant], [Arg29 As Variant], [Arg30 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Creates subtotals.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A number indicating the aggregation function to be used by the method.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The first Range object for which a subtotal is to be calculated.

methods.name: SumIf
methods.signature: SumIf(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant, [Arg3 As Variant]) As Double
methods.description: Adds the cells specified by a given criteria.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Range - the range of cells that you want evaluated by criteria.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Criteria - the criteria in the form of a number, expression, or text that defines which cells will be added. For example, criteria can be expressed as 32, "32", ">32", or "apples".

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Sum_range - the actual cells to add if their corresponding cells in range match criteria. If sum_range is omitted, the cells in range are both evaluated by criteria and added if they match criteria.

methods.name: CountIf
methods.signature: CountIf(Arg1 As Range, Arg2 As Variant) As Double
methods.description: Counts the number of cells within a range that meet the given criteria.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The range of cells from which you want to count cells.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: The criteria in the form of a number, expression, cell reference, or text that defines which cells will be counted. For example, criteria can be expressed as 32, "32", ">32", "apples", or B4.

methods.name: CountBlank
methods.description: Counts empty cells in a specified range of cells.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The range from which you want to count the blank cells.

methods.name: Ispmt
methods.signature: Ispmt(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double) As Double
methods.description: Calculates the interest paid during a specific period of an investment. This function is provided for compatibility with Lotus 1-2-3.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Rate - the interest rate for the investment.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Per - the period for which you want to find the interest; must be between 1 and nper.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Nper - the total number of payment periods for the investment.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Pv - the present value of the investment. For a loan, pv is the loan amount.

methods.name: Roman
methods.signature: Roman(Arg1 As Double, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts an arabic numeral to roman, as text.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the Arabic numeral that you want converted.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Form - a number specifying the type of roman numeral you want. The roman numeral style ranges from Classic to Simplified, becoming more concise as the value of form increases.

methods.name: Asc
methods.description: For double-byte character set (DBCS) languages, changes full-width (double-byte) characters to half-width (single-byte) characters.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The text or a reference to a cell that contains the text that you want to change. If the text does not contain any full-width letters, the text is not changed.

methods.name: Dbcs
methods.description: Converts half-width (single-byte) letters within a character string to full-width (double-byte) characters. The name of the function (and the characters that it converts) depends upon the language settings. Read/write String.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: The text or a reference to a cell that contains the text that you want to change.

methods.name: Phonetic
methods.description: Extracts the phonetic (furigana) characters from a text string.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Reference - a text string or a reference to a single cell or a range of cells that contain a furigana text string.

methods.name: BahtText
methods.description: Converts a number to Thai text and adds a suffix of Baht.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: A number that you want to convert to text, or a reference to a cell containing a number, or a formula that evaluates to a number.

methods.description: This method connects to a source to receive real-time data (RTD).

parameters.name: progID
parameters.description: A string representing the real-time server programmatic identifier.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: A server name, Null string, or vbNullString constant.

parameters.name: topic1
parameters.description: A String representing a topic.

methods.name: Hex2Bin
methods.signature: Hex2Bin(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts a hexadecimal number to binary.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the hexadecimal number that you want to convert. Number cannot contain more than 10 characters. The most significant bit of number is the sign bit (40th bit from the right). The remaining 9 bits are magnitude bits. Negative numbers are represented using two's-complement notation.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Places - the number of characters to use. If places is omitted, Hex2Bin uses the minimum number of characters necessary. Places is useful for padding the return value with leading 0s (zeros).

methods.name: Hex2Dec
methods.description: Converts a hexadecimal number to decimal.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the hexadecimal number that you want to convert. Number cannot contain more than 10 characters (40 bits). The most significant bit of number is the sign bit. The remaining 39 bits are magnitude bits. Negative numbers are represented using two's-complement notation.

methods.name: Hex2Oct
methods.signature: Hex2Oct(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts a hexadecimal number to octal.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the hexadecimal number that you want to convert. Number cannot contain more than 10 characters. The most significant bit of number is the sign bit. The remaining 39 bits are magnitude bits. Negative numbers are represented using two's-complement notation.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Places - the number of characters to use. If places is omitted, Hex2Oct uses the minimum number of characters necessary. Places is useful for padding the return value with leading 0s (zeros).

methods.name: Dec2Bin
methods.signature: Dec2Bin(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts a decimal number to binary.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the decimal integer that you want to convert. If number is negative, valid place values are ignored and Dec2Bin returns a 10-character (10-bit) binary number in which the most significant bit is the sign bit. The remaining 9 bits are magnitude bits. Negative numbers are represented using two's-complement notation.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Places - the number of characters to use. If places is omitted, Dec2Bin uses the minimum number of characters necessary. Places is useful for padding the return value with leading 0s (zeros).

methods.name: Dec2Hex
methods.signature: Dec2Hex(Arg1 As Variant, [Arg2 As Variant]) As String
methods.description: Converts a decimal number to hexadecimal.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number - the decimal integer that you want to convert. If number is negative, places is ignored and Dec2Hex returns a 10-character (40-bit) hexadecimal number in which the most significant bit is the sign bit. The remaining 39 bits are magnitude bits. Negative numbers are represented using two's-complement notation.

parameters.name: Arg2

methods.name: HypGeom_Dist
methods.signature: HypGeom_Dist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Double, Arg5 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the hypergeometric distribution. HypGeom_Dist returns the probability of a given number of sample successes, given the sample size, population successes, and population size. Use HypGeom_Dist for problems with a finite population, where each observation is either a success or a failure, and where each subset of a given size is chosen with equal likelihood.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Sample_s - the number of successes in the sample.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Number_sample - the size of the sample.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Population_s - the number of successes in the population.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Number_population - the population size.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Cumulative - a logical value that determines the form of the function. If cumulative is True, HypGeom_Dist returns the cumulative distribution function; if False, it returns the probability mass function.

methods.name: NegBinom_Dist
methods.signature: NegBinom_Dist(Arg1 As Double, Arg2 As Double, Arg3 As Double, Arg4 As Boolean) As Double
methods.description: Returns the negative binomial distribution. NegBinom_Dist returns the probability that there will be number_f failures before the number_s-th success, when the constant probability of a success is probability_s. This function is similar to the binomial distribution, except that the number of successes is fixed, and the number of trials is variable. Like the binomial, trials are assumed to be independent.

parameters.name: Arg1
parameters.description: Number_f - the number of failures.

parameters.name: Arg2
parameters.description: Number_s - the threshold number of successes.

parameters.name: Arg3
parameters.description: Probability_s - the probability of a success.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Cumulative - A logical value that determines the form of the function. If cumulative is True, NegBinom_Dist returns the cumulative distribution function; if False, it returns the probability density function.

parameters.description: Statistic_type: A numeric value between 1 and 8, indicating which statistic will be returned for the calculated forecast.

parameters.name: Arg4
parameters.description: Confidence level: A numerical value between 0 and 1 (exclusive), indicating a confidence level for the calculated confidence interval. See Remarks.

parameters.name: Arg5
parameters.description: Data completions: Although the timeline requires a constant step between data points, Forecast_ETS_STAT supports up to 30% missing data, and automatically adjusts for it. See Remarks.

parameters.name: Arg6
parameters.description: Aggregation: Although the timeline requires a constant step between data points, Forecast_ETS_STAT aggregates multiple points that have the same time stamp. See Remarks.

types.name: Worksheets
types.description: A collection of all the Worksheet objects in the specified or active workbook. Each Worksheet object represents a worksheet.
types.remarks: The Worksheet object is also a member of the Sheets collection. The Sheets collection contains all the sheets in the workbook (both chart sheets and worksheets).
types.example: Worksheets.Move After:=Sheets(Sheets.Count)

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Count
properties.description: Returns a Long value that represents the number of objects in the collection.

properties.name: Item
properties.description: Returns a single object from a collection.

properties.name: HPageBreaks
properties.description: Returns an HPageBreaks collection that represents the horizontal page breaks on the sheet. Read-only.

properties.name: VPageBreaks
properties.description: Returns a VPageBreaks collection that represents the vertical page breaks on the sheet. Read-only.

properties.name: Visible
properties.description: Returns or sets a Variant value that determines whether the object is visible.

methods.name: Add
methods.signature: Add([Before As Variant], [After As Variant], [Count As Variant], [Type As Variant]) As Object
methods.description: Creates a new worksheet, chart, or macro sheet. The new worksheet becomes the active sheet.

parameters.name: Before
parameters.description: An object that specifies the sheet before which the new sheet is added.

parameters.name: After
parameters.description: An object that specifies the sheet after which the new sheet is added.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: The number of sheets to be added. The default value is one.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Specifies the sheet type. Can be one of the following XlSheetType constants: xlWorksheet, xlChart, xlExcel4MacroSheet, or xlExcel4IntlMacroSheet. If you are inserting a sheet based on an existing template, specify the path to the template. The default value is xlWorksheet.

methods.name: Copy
methods.description: Copies the sheet to another location in the workbook.

parameters.name: Before
parameters.description: The sheet before which the copied sheet will be placed. You cannot specify _Before_ if you specify _After_.

parameters.name: After
parameters.description: The sheet after which the copied sheet will be placed. You cannot specify _After_ if you specify _Before_.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description: Deletes the object.

methods.name: FillAcrossSheets
methods.description: Copies a range to the same area on all other worksheets in a collection.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: The range to fill on all the worksheets in the collection. The range must be from a worksheet within the collection.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Specifies how to copy the range.

methods.name: Move
methods.description: Moves the sheet to another location in the workbook.

parameters.name: Before
parameters.description: The sheet before which the moved sheet will be placed. You cannot specify _Before_ if you specify _After_.

parameters.name: After
parameters.description: The sheet after which the moved sheet will be placed. You cannot specify _After_ if you specify _Before_.

methods.name: PrintPreview
methods.description: Shows a preview of the object as it would look when printed.

parameters.name: EnableChanges
parameters.description: Pass a Boolean value to specify if the user can change the margins and other page setup options available in print preview.

methods.name: Select
methods.description: Selects the object.

parameters.name: Replace
parameters.description: Used only with sheets. True to replace the current selection with the specified object. False to extend the current selection to include any previously selected objects and the specified object.

methods.name: PrintOut
methods.signature: PrintOut([From As Variant], [To As Variant], [Copies As Variant], [Preview As Variant], [ActivePrinter As Variant], [PrintToFile As Variant], [Collate As Variant], [PrToFileName As Variant], [IgnorePrintAreas As Variant])
methods.description: Prints the object.

parameters.name: From
parameters.description: The number of the page at which to start printing. If this argument is omitted, printing starts at the beginning.

parameters.name: To
parameters.description: The number of the last page to print. If this argument is omitted, printing ends with the last page.

parameters.name: Copies
parameters.description: The number of copies to print. If this argument is omitted, one copy is printed.

parameters.name: Preview
parameters.description: True to have Microsoft Excel invoke print preview before printing the object. False (or omitted) to print the object immediately.

parameters.name: ActivePrinter
parameters.description: Sets the name of the active printer.

parameters.name: PrintToFile
parameters.description: True to print to a file. If _PrToFileName_ is not specified, Microsoft Excel prompts the user to enter the name of the output file.

parameters.name: Collate
parameters.description: True to collate multiple copies.

parameters.name: PrToFileName
parameters.description: If _PrintToFile_ is set to True, this argument specifies the name of the file that you want to print to.

parameters.name: IgnorePrintAreas
parameters.description: True to ignore print areas and print the entire object.

methods.name: Add2
methods.signature: Add2([Before As Variant], [After As Variant], [Count As Variant], [NewLayout As Variant]) As Object

types.name: XmlMap
types.description: Represents an XML map that has been added to a workbook.
types.remarks: Use the Add method of the XmlMaps collection to add an XML map to a workbook. Use the Import method to import XML data from an XML data file into cells mapped to the specified XmlMap. The ImportXml method imports XML data for a String variable. Use the Export method to export data from cells mapped to the specified XmlMap. The ExportXml method exports XML data to a String variable.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Returns or sets a String value that represents the friendly name used to uniquely identify a mapping in the workbook.

properties.name: IsExportable
properties.description: Returns True if Microsoft Excel can use the XPath objects in the specified schema map to export XML data, and all XML lists mapped to the specified schema map can be exported.

properties.name: ShowImportExportValidationErrors
properties.description: Returns or sets whether to display a dialog box that details schema-validation errors when data is imported or exported through the specified XML schema map. The default value is False. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: SaveDataSourceDefinition
properties.description: True if the data source definition of the specified XML schema map is saved with the workbook. The default value is True. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: AdjustColumnWidth
properties.description: True if the column widths are automatically adjusted for the best fit each time that you refresh the specified XML map.

properties.name: PreserveColumnFilter
properties.description: Returns or sets whether filtering is preserved when the specified XML map is refreshed. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: PreserveNumberFormatting
properties.description: True if number formatting on cells mapped to the specified XML schema map are preserved when the schema map is refreshed. The default value is False. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: AppendOnImport
properties.description: True if you want to append new rows to XML lists that are bound to the specified schema map when you are importing new data or refreshing an existing connection.

properties.name: RootElementName
properties.description: Returns a String that represents the name of the root element for the specified XML schema map. Read-only.

properties.name: RootElementNamespace
properties.description: Returns an XmlNamespace object that represents the root element for the specified XML schema map. Read-only.

properties.name: Schemas
properties.description: Returns an XmlSchemas collection that represents the schemas that the specified XmlMap object contains. Read-only.

properties.name: DataBinding
properties.description: Returns an XmlDataBinding object that represents the binding associated with the specified schema map. Read-only.

properties.name: WorkbookConnection
properties.description: Returns a new connection for the specified XMLMap object. Read-only.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description: Removes the specified XML map from the workbook.

methods.name: Import
methods.signature: Import(Url As String, [Overwrite As Variant]) As XlXmlImportResult
methods.description: Imports data from the specified XML data file into cells that have been mapped to the specified XmlMap object.

parameters.name: Url
parameters.description: The path to the XML data to import. The path can be specified in Universal Naming convention (UNC) or Uniform Resource Locator (URL) format. The file can be an XML data file.

parameters.name: Overwrite
parameters.description: Set to True to overwrite existing data. Set to False to append to existing data. The default value is False.

methods.name: ImportXml
methods.signature: ImportXml(XmlData As String, [Overwrite As Variant]) As XlXmlImportResult
methods.description: Imports XML data from a String variable into cells that have been mapped to the specified XmlMap object.

parameters.name: XmlData
parameters.description: The string that contains the XML data to import.

parameters.name: Overwrite
parameters.description: Specifies whether to overwrite the contents of cells that are currently mapped to the specified XML map. Set to True to overwrite the cells; set to False to append the data to the existing range.

methods.name: Export
methods.signature: Export(Url As String, [Overwrite As Variant]) As XlXmlExportResult
methods.description: Exports the contents of cells mapped to the specified XmlMap object to an XML data file.

parameters.name: Url
parameters.description: The path and file name of the XML data file to export to.

parameters.name: Overwrite
parameters.description: Set to True to overwrite the file specified in the _Url_ parameter if the file exists. The default value is False.

methods.name: ExportXml
methods.description: Exports the contents of cells mapped to the specified XmlMap object to a String variable.

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description: The variable to export the data to.

types.name: XmlMaps
types.description: Represents the collection of XmlMap objects that have been added to a workbook.
types.example:
Sub AddXmlMap()
 Dim strSchemaLocation As String

 strSchemaLocation = "https://example.microsoft.com/schemas/CustomerData.xsd"
 ActiveWorkbook.XmlMaps.Add strSchemaLocation, "Root"
End Sub

methods.signature: Add(Schema As String, [RootElementName As Variant]) As XmlMap
methods.description: Adds an XML map to the specified workbook.

parameters.name: Schema
parameters.description: The schema to be added as an XML map. The string can be a path to a schema file, or the schema itself. The path can be specified in the Universal Naming Convention (UNC) or Uniform Resource Locator (URL) format.

parameters.name: RootElementName
parameters.description: The name of the root element. This argument can be ignored if the schema contains only one root element.

types.name: XmlNamespace
types.description: Represents a namespace that has been added to a workbook.
types.remarks: Use the Prefix property to return the prefix of an XmlNamespace object. Use the Uri property to return the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) of an XmlNamespace object.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Uri
properties.description: Returns a String that represents the Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) for the specified XML namespace. Read-only.

properties.name: Prefix
properties.description: Returns a String that represents the prefix for the specified XML namespace. Read-only.

types.name: XmlNamespaces
types.description: Represents the collection of XmlNamespace objects in a workbook.
types.remarks: Use the Item method to access a particular XmlNamespace object. Use the Value property to return a String that lists the namespaces that have been added to a workbook.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Item
properties.description: Returns a single object from a collection.

properties.name: Count
properties.description: Returns a Long value that represents the number of objects in the collection.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Returns a String value that represents the XML namespaces that have been added to the workbook.

methods.name: InstallManifest
methods.description: Installs the specified XML expansion pack on the user's computer, making an XML smart document solution available to one or more users.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The path and file name of the XML expansion pack.

parameters.name: InstallForAllUsers
parameters.description: True installs the XML expansion pack and makes it available to all users on a machine. False makes the XML expansion pack available for the current user only. The default is False.

types.name: XmlSchema
types.description: Represents an XML schema contained by an XmlMap object.
types.remarks: Use the Item method to return an XmlSchema object from the XmlSchemas collection. Use the Namespace property to return the target namespace for a schema. Use the XML property to return the XML contents of a schema.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Namespace
properties.description: Returns an XmlNamespace object that represents the target namespace for the specified schema. Read-only.

properties.name: XML
properties.description: Returns a String value that represents the content of the specified schema.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Returns a String value that represents the friendly name used to identify an XML schema in an XmlMap object.

types.name: XmlSchemas
types.description: Represents the collection of XmlSchema objects contained by an XmlMap object.
types.remarks: Use the Schemas property of the XmlMap object to return the XmlSchemas collection. Use the Item property to return an XmlSchema object from the XmlSchemas collection.

properties.name: Creator

properties.name: Parent

properties.name: Count

types.name: XPath
types.description: Represents an XPath that has been mapped to a Range or ListColumn object.
types.remarks: Use the SetValue method to map an XPath to a range or list column. The SetValue method is also used to change the properties of an existing XPath. Use the Clear method to remove an XPath that has been mapped to a range or list column.
types.example:
Sub CreateXMLList()
 Dim mapContact As XmlMap
 Dim strXPath As String
 Dim lstContacts As ListObject
 Dim lcNewCol As ListColumn

 ' Specify the schema map to use.
 Set mapContact = ActiveWorkbook.XmlMaps("Contacts")

 ' Create a new list.
 Set lstContacts = ActiveSheet.ListObjects.Add

 ' Specify the first element to map.
 strXPath = "/Root/Person/FirstName"
 ' Map the element.
 lstContacts.ListColumns(1).XPath.SetValue mapContact, strXPath

 ' Specify the element to map.
 strXPath = "/Root/Person/LastName"
 ' Add a column to the list.
 Set lcNewCol = lstContacts.ListColumns.Add
 ' Map the element.
 lcNewCol.XPath.SetValue mapContact, strXPath

 strXPath = "/Root/Person/Address/Zip"
 Set lcNewCol = lstContacts.ListColumns.Add
 lcNewCol.XPath.SetValue mapContact, strXPath
End Sub

properties.name: Application
properties.description: When used without an object qualifier, this property returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Excel application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which this object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns the parent object for the specified object. Read-only.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Returns a String that represents the XPath for the specified object.

properties.name: Map
properties.description: Returns an XmlMap object that represents the schema map that contains the specified XPath object. Read-only.

properties.name: Repeating
properties.description: Returns True if the specified XPath object is mapped to an XML list; returns False if the XPath object is mapped to a single cell. Read-only Boolean.

methods.name: SetValue
methods.signature: SetValue(Map As XmlMap, XPath As String, [SelectionNamespace As Variant], [Repeating As Variant])
methods.description: Maps the specified XPath object to a ListColumn object or Range collection. If the XPath object has previously been mapped to the ListColumn object or Range collection, the SetValue method sets the properties of the XPath object.

parameters.name: Map
parameters.description: The map info that the mapped range will be associated with.

parameters.name: XPath
parameters.description: A valid XPath expression that tells Excel what XML data should appear in this mapped range. The XPath string can also contain valid filters, in which case, only a subset of the data that the XPath points to will ever appear in this mapped range.

parameters.name: SelectionNamespace
parameters.description: Specifies any namespace prefixes used in the _XPath_ argument. This argument can be omitted if the XPath object doesn't contain any prefixes, or if the XPath object uses the Microsoft Excel internal prefixes.

parameters.name: Repeating
parameters.description: Specifies whether the XPath object is to be bound to a column in an XML list or mapped to a single cell. Set to True to bind the XPath object to a column in an XML list. False forces a non-repeating cell to be created. If the range is greater than a single cell and False is specified, a run-time error occurs.

methods.name: Clear
methods.description: Clears all XPath schema information for the mapped range.
